books.section: Topic 2.5 Interactions Between American Indians and Europeans
The Early Colonial Era: Spain Colonizes the New World

options.text: Spanish authorities accommodated certain aspects of Pueblo culture in the late 1600s and 1700s.

options.misconception: The Pueblo peoples survived; they were not eliminated.
options.text: Spanish armies and disease completely eliminated the Pueblo population of the Southwest.

options.misconception: Spain reconquered New Mexico in the 1690s; it did not abandon North America.
options.text: Defeated by the rebels, Spain permanently abandoned all its territorial claims in North America by 1700.

options.misconception: Spain and Britain remained rivals; they did not ally to control the interior.
options.text: Spain and Britain allied to impose joint European control over the interior of North America.

rationales.A: The revolt changed the terms of Spanish rule. After the reconquest of the 1690s, Spanish authorities tolerated traditional religious practices they had once violently suppressed and eased the forced-labor demands — because the lesson of 1680 was that severity had failed. Accommodation, not coercion, was what held the province afterward, and the Pueblo peoples kept their ceremonies because they had fought for them.
rationales.B: The Pueblo peoples survived; they were not eliminated.
rationales.C: Spain reconquered New Mexico in the 1690s; it did not abandon North America.
rationales.D: Spain and Britain remained rivals; they did not ally to control the interior.
rationales.general:
1. Ask what changed after the revolt. The Spanish returned in the 1690s, but they did not return to the old rules.
2. Name the change. Traditional practices were tolerated, and the forced-labor demands eased.
3. Ask why. Background: the lesson of 1680 was that severity had failed, so accommodation was what held the province.
Remember: a revolt can win even after it loses — if the rulers who return have learned not to repeat it.

source: original; stimulus paraphrased from the 1681 interrogation of Josephe
stem: Which of the following best describes Spanish policy in the region in the decades after the events Josephe describes?

stimulus.source_note: Paraphrase of the 1681 interrogation of Josephe.
stimulus.text: Asked what drove the rebels to renounce Spanish authority, Josephe — a Spanish-speaking Pueblo Indian questioned by colonial officials after the 1680 uprising — answered that the causes were the ill treatment they suffered: Spanish officials beat them, seized their property, and forced them to work without pay. Asked why the rebels burned churches and images, mocked sacred objects, and killed priests, Josephe said he had heard it stated that while besieging the Spanish villa the rebels shouted that the Spaniards' God was dead and that only their own gods lived. Their captains ordered that the names of Jesus and Mary never be spoken, and Josephe reported seeing new houses of native worship built where the people danced their traditional ceremonial dances. — paraphrased from the 1681 interrogation of Josephe
